title: 2 hospitalized after CN Rail train derails into Skeena River near Terrace, B.C.
summary: Police say injuries are not life-threatening and cleanup is underway.

image.caption: CN Rail says five of its cars came off the track near Terrace, B.C., on Nov. 17, 2026, falling into the Skeena River. It says no dangerous goods were on board. (Carl J. Reibin)

blocks.text: Police say injuries are not life-threatening and cleanup is underway.
Injuries are not life-threatening, police say
Two people were taken to hospital after a CN Rail train went off the tracks in northwest B.C. and plunged into the Skeena River.
RCMP say the injuries are non-life-threatening, and cleanup is underway.
Emergency vehicles closed Highway 16 west of Terrace shortly after 1 p.m. PT as police, ambulance and fire crews responded.
It has since been reopened to single-lane alternating traffic.
Multiple emergency vehicles responded to a CN Rail incident west of Terrace, B.C., on Nov. 17, 2026. (Gordon Bonenfant)
Highway 16 is the main artery connecting Terrace to Prince Rupert, where Canada's third-busiest port is used to ship product transported by train and truck to overseas markets.
CN Rail has not said what was on board the train at the time of the derailment, but in a statement said "there are no fires, no dangerous goods and no impact to public safety."
It says one locomotive and five cars derailed. Images from the scene appear to show multiple cars off the track.
Police, ministry of transportation and CN Rail officials remain on the scene.
CN Rail says there were no dangerous goods on the train. (Carl J. Reibin)
